title: Dectin-1 recognizes bacterial EF-Tu during infection
projectDescription: Dectin-1 (CLEC7A) is a pattern-recognition receptor known for its essential role in antifungal defense, and may also be associated with antibacterial immunity. Here we show that in murine pneumonia models, Dectin-1 deficiency impaired pulmonary clearance of Streptococcus pneu-moniae and Haemophilus influenzae. This susceptibility was gene-dose-dependent, with hetero-zygous (Clec7a+/–) and knockout (Clec7a–/–) mice exhibiting higher bacterial burdens and al-tered immune responses compared to wild-type mice. Translating these findings to humans, analysis of 28,175 genome-sequenced individuals showed that the loss-of-function CLEC7A variant Y238X (rs16910526) was associated with increased risk of bacterial pneumonia. Affini-ty purification followed by mass spectrometry identified bacterial elongation factor Tu (EF-Tu) as a conserved Dectin-1 ligand. EF-Tu bound the Dectin-1 carbohydrate-recognition domain and, when clustered, activated downstream NF-κB signaling. These findings establish EF-Tu as a pathogen-associated molecular pattern and define Dectin-1 as an innate receptor controlling antibacterial inflammation and host susceptibility to pneumonia.
sampleProcessingProtocol: NiMag bead coating MagneHis™ nickel beads (Promega, Madison, WI, USA) were separated from storage buffer using a DynaMag™-2 magnetic rack (Thermo Fisher, Uppsala, Sweden) and washed 3 times with 500 µL PBS. Purified protein was added at the desired protein-to-bead ratio. For the un-coated control, PBS was added instead of protein. Beads were incubated overnight at 4 °C on a rolling table. After incubation, the supernatant was removed, beads were washed as above, re-suspended in PBS, and stored at 4 °C. Coating efficiency was assessed by SDS-PAGE (Supple-mentary Fig. 5). Affinity purification-mass spectrometry NTHi 3655 was cultured in BHI medium supplemented with NAD and hemin (2 μg/mL each) to mid-log phase (OD₆₀₀ ≈ 0.5). Bacteria were harvested, washed with PBS, and resuspended in lysis buffer (PBS, 10 mM imidazole) to an OD₆₀₀ of 5. Cells were lysed by sonication (Biorup-tor) and the lysate was clarified by centrifugation twice (16,000 × g, 4°C). For affinity purifica-tion, MagneHis™ Ni-NTA magnetic beads (V8560; Promega) were coated with recombinant human Dectin-1a (CLEC7A) overnight at 4°C in coating buffer (PBS, 0.5 M NaCl, 10 mM imid-azole). As controls, parallel samples included empty beads incubated with lysate and Dectin-1-coated beads incubated without lysate. Coated beads were incubated with 442 µg of bacterial lysate protein overnight at 4°C. After incubation, beads were washed three times with wash buffer (PBS, 10 mM imidazole), and bound proteins were eluted with elution buffer (PBS, 500 mM imidazole). Eluates were pooled for mass spectrometry analysis. Three biological replicates were performed for each condition. Prior to MS analysis, samples were digested with trypsin using a modified filter-aided sample preparation (FASP) protocol (53). Briefly, samples were denatured in 8 M urea, 100 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.0) and reduced with 15 mM DTT, then loaded onto 10 kDa microfiltration filters (Microcon-10, Merck Millipore). Proteins were alkylated with 15 mM iodoacetamide in 100 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.0) and washed extensively with 100 mM ammonium bicarbonate. Digestion was performed with trypsin (Merck) at 37°C for 16 h. Tryptic peptides were recovered by micro-purification before MS analysis. Peptides were analyzed using an EASY-nLC 1200 system (Thermo Scientific) coupled to an Orbitrap Eclipse Tribrid Mass Spectrometer (Thermo Scientific). The setup included a 2 cm trap column (100 μm i.d.) and a 15 cm analytical column (75 μm i.d.), both packed in-house with ReproSil-Pur C18-AQ 3 μm resin (Dr. Maisch GmbH). Peptides were eluted at 250 nL/min using a 35-min gradient from 6% to 44% phase B (0.1% formic acid, 80% acetonitrile), fol-lowed by a 30 s ramp to 100% B and 5 min at 100% B.
dataProcessingProtocol: Protein identification and quantification were performed using Proteome Discoverer 2.5 (Ther-mo Scientific). Data were searched against UniProt proteomes of Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) (v2024-01-24), Haemophilus influenzae 3655 (v2024-01-24), and Homo sapiens (v2023-06-28). Search parameters: Precursor mass tolerance: 10 ppm, Fragment mass tolerance: 0.02 Da, Static modification: Carbamidomethyl (+57.021 Da, C), Dynamic modification: Oxidation (+15.995 Da, M) and Enzyme: Trypsin, allowing 1 missed cleavage.  Peptides and proteins were filtered to a 1% FDR using a target-decoy strategy with Ben-jamini-Hochberg correction. Label-free quantification was based on unique peptides only. Pro-teins quantified by fewer than three unique peptides or specific to E. coli were excluded from further analysis. Enrichment was assessed by calculating the fold-change between Dectin-1-coated beads and empty bead controls, with relative protein abundance expressed in parts per million. Proteins were considered significantly enriched if they had an adjusted p-value <0.05 (Benjamini-Hochberg correction) and were detected in all three biological replicates.
